title: Cold rebuild: the inbox
summary: Rebuild the inbox from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built the **inbox** in *Idempotent consumers, dedup keys and Kafka exactly-once*.
Now write it again from an **empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the
ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing it;
rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, go back to the lesson, then try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Warm-up: the inbox keys are tuples. What does this print?
explain: Value tuples compare by their items, so `("billing", "m-1")` twice is the same key, and the same message id for a
different consumer is a different key.

steps.title: Rebuild the inbox cold
prompt: Write a class `Inbox`. Everything one call does is a single transaction: all of it is recorded, or none of it.

3. record `(consumer, messageId)`; if this consumer already charged `orderId` → `"already charged"`;
